intelligence.human_view: Records are supposed to sit still until someone changes them. These did not. The apex and www AAAA records for nayanet.app were there at 02:55Z and gone by 03:25Z — no change event, no hand, no attribution — and the domain answered NXDOMAIN in between. The right recovery is not to redesign the DNS or to guess at new values: it is to put back exactly what was verified before, the 2026-11-03 four-record state, and then to prove it three times over with fresh fetches that return 200. That is the discipline this incident teaches: keep a verified state on record, because the day a record vanishes without a cause is the day the verified state is the only thing you can trust. And say plainly what is not known — the vanishing is unattributed — rather than inventing a cause to close the story.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine the address of your house suddenly disappears from the map, and nobody erased it. That's what happened — the address records just vanished. The fix wasn't to make up a new address. It was to put back the exact address that was written down and checked before — the one from November 3rd — and then knock on the door three times to make sure someone answers. Always keep a good copy of the address written down, because sometimes things disappear for no reason anyone can see.
